questions.title: What role does exponential gating play in sLSTM's ability to revise stored values?
questions.question_body: In the sLSTM forward equations (Eq. 5), the input and forget gates use exponential activation. How exactly does this allow the network to overwrite or revise a previously stored value when a more similar key is encountered, as claimed when solving the Nearest Neighbor Search task? Is it purely a matter of larger gate values or also the normalizer state?

questions.title: Why is the normalizer state required in the sLSTM and mLSTM equations?
questions.question_body: Both sLSTM and mLSTM introduce a normalizer state (n_t) that accumulates weighted sums of gates. I understand it’s for normalization, but could someone explain, mathematically, how it prevents the hidden-state activation from blowing up when many past keys have been summed? What happens if we omit n_t?

questions.title: How does the mLSTM matrix memory compare to the Transformer self‑attention key‑value matrix?
questions.question_body: The mLSTM cell stores a matrix C_t = C_{t-1} + v_t k_t^T. This looks similar to the QKV attention formulation. Could someone clarify the exact relationship? For instance, does retrieving C_t q_t correspond to a dot‑product attention with a single previous key? How does the capacity of mLSTM scale with dimension d compared to a Transformer with d‑dimensional keys?

questions.title: Can sLSTM be parallelized if we drop memory mixing?
questions.question_body: The paper states that sLSTM’s hidden‐hidden recurrent connections prevent parallel execution, whereas mLSTM is fully parallelizable. If we were to remove the memory mixing (i.e., set R_z, R_i, R_f, R_o to zero), would sLSTM then become equivalent to mLSTM? Would we lose any expressive power?

questions.title: Why is the stabilizer state m_t defined as a max of log‑gate terms?
questions.question_body: Equation (7) defines m_t = max(log(f_t)+m_{t‑1}, log(i_t)). This seems reminiscent of a log‑sum‑exp trick, but with a max instead. What numerical instability does it avert, and how does the subsequent re‑exponentiation in (8) guarantee that the overall forward pass remains unchanged?

questions.title: How are the gating parameters initialized to ensure stable training of xLSTM?
questions.question_body: Appendix mentions careful initialization of forget gates. What is the recommended strategy for initializing the learnable weights w_f and biases b_f in both sLSTM and mLSTM? Does this differ from standard LSTM initializations, and what happen if we use the same as vanilla LSTM?

questions.title: What exactly does 'memory mixing' mean in the context of sLSTM?
questions.question_body: The paper states that new sLSTM can mix memory across cells via recurrent matrices R_z, R_i, R_f, R_o, and that memory mixing is a new feature. Could someone formalize what operations are performed on the cell state vector when multiple cells are present? How does this differ from the inter‑cell mixing used in standard multi‑dimensional LSTM?

questions.title: Why is mLSTM considered to have constant memory complexity with sequence length?
questions.question_body: The authors claim that the memory of mLSTM is linear in context length while being constant with respect to sequence length. Since C_t is a d×d matrix independent of t, does this mean that each time step requires O(d^2) operations but no extra storage per time‑step? How does this compare to Transformers where the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length?

questions.title: How does the choice of the ratio a:b in xLSTM[a:b] affect model performance?
questions.question_body: The paper introduces a notation xLSTM[a:b] to indicate the proportion of mLSTM to sLSTM blocks. What are the practical guidelines for selecting a:b? Does a higher proportion of mLSTM always lead to better perplexity, or are there trade‑offs in terms of memory capacity versus state tracking?

questions.title: Can xLSTM be combined with attention mechanisms?
questions.question_body: Some modern LLMs combine recurrent layers with attention (e.g., LM‑U). Would it be straightforward to add a standard self‑attention module on top of xLSTM blocks, or would the exponential gating interfere with attention weighting? Has any attempt been made to hybridize the two?
